However, cooperation is a challenge because the costs of cooperation are often incurred early on, but the benefits are only realized later, creating an incentive to defect. How can AI agents cooperate with commitment? Here, we draw on inspiration from legal institutions and contracting that human societies have used to solve principal-agent problems of this kind. Contracts provide observable representations of agreements that enable credible commitments through the enforcement of terms. We study the role of contract-based cooperation using LLM-based agents in \CT, a spatial-temporal game that combines bargaining with navigation towards a goal. We study a suite of contract representations that range from formal contracts that compile to code to natural contracts that require reinterpretation. We evaluate agents with a range of LLM backbones using different sizes and providers. We find that self-negotiated contracts can improve cooperative outcomes beyond what is possible with regular trading.

AI.tldr: LLM-based agents use self-negotiated contracts (from formal code to natural language) to improve cooperative outcomes in spatial-temporal bargaining games, drawing inspiration from human legal institutions to solve principal-agent problems.
AI.motivation: As AI agents gain autonomy in multi-agent environments, they need to learn cooperation with humans and other agents. The core challenge is that cooperation costs occur early while benefits are delayed, creating incentives to defect - a classic principal-agent problem.
AI.method: The authors study contract-based cooperation using LLM-based agents in a spatial-temporal game (CT) that combines bargaining with navigation toward goals. They test a suite of contract representations ranging from formal contracts that compile to code to natural contracts requiring reinterpretation. Various LLM backbones (different sizes and providers) are evaluated.
AI.result: Self-negotiated contracts can improve cooperative outcomes beyond what's possible with regular trading. The study shows that contract-based approaches effectively enhance cooperation among AI agents in complex multi-agent scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Contract-based cooperation, inspired by human legal institutions, provides an effective mechanism for AI agents to make credible commitments and improve cooperative outcomes in multi-agent systems, addressing the temporal mismatch between cooperation costs and benefits.

title: Topological Data Analysis and Graph-Theoretic Approaches for Tennis Match Prediction
summary: We present two approaches for predicting tennis match outcomes using topological data analysis and graph theory on ATP singles matches from 2000-2025. The first method applies lower-star filtration to player competitive networks, extracting topological features through persistent homology using four summary methods (VAB, HNAV, HWNAV, OW-HNPV) combined with Modified Band Depth analysis. Algorithmic optimizations including ego graph approximations and triangle elimination enable analysis of about 66k matches. Our Random Forest model achieves 66.2% accuracy (AUC = 0.719) using topological, graph-theoretic, and ranking features. Feature importance analysis reveals that rankings contribute 36.3%, centralities 25.5%, and TDA features 24.0%, with topological features providing complementary signal. When rankings are unavailable, the topology-only model maintains 63.56% accuracy, demonstrating that network-derived features alone capture meaningful competitive structure. The second method uses a modified Katz similarity index with temporal edge weighting, achieving 62.48% accuracy on held-out test data. This work represents the first application of lower-star filtration to tennis prediction, provides systematic comparison of four topological summary methods in sports analytics, and demonstrates that TDA can achieve above-chance prediction using network topology alone while providing additional value when combined with traditional features.

AI.tldr: Topological Data Analysis applied to tennis match prediction achieves 66.2% accuracy by combining network topology with traditional features, with network-only approaches still performing above chance (63.56%).
AI.motivation: There is a need for novel approaches to predict tennis match outcomes that go beyond traditional statistical features, leveraging the competitive network structure between players and applying topological methods that haven't been explored in this domain.
AI.method: Two approaches: 1) Lower-star filtration on player competitive networks with persistent homology using four summary methods (VAB, HNAV, HWNAV, OW-HNPV) combined with Modified Band Depth analysis, plus algorithmic optimizations like ego graph approximations; 2) Modified Katz similarity index with temporal edge weighting. Both methods use Random Forest models on ATP singles match data (2000-2025).
AI.result: Random Forest model achieves 66.2% accuracy (AUC = 0.719) with feature importance: rankings 36.3%, centralities 25.5%, TDA features 24.0%. Topology-only model without rankings maintains 63.56% accuracy. Modified Katz similarity method achieves 62.48% accuracy on held-out data.
AI.conclusion: This work represents the first application of lower-star filtration to tennis prediction, demonstrates that TDA features provide complementary signal to traditional features, and shows network topology alone can achieve above-chance prediction, opening new avenues for sports analytics.

title: Disentangling Multi-View Scanning in Mamba for Network Traffic Anomaly Detection
summary: Network Traffic Anomaly Detection (NTAD) is a critical task in cybersecurity, yet timely and accurate anomaly detection remains challenging. Mamba has emerged as a particularly promising backbone for NTAD due to its linear-time complexity for long-sequence modeling. It further incorporates a dedicated multi-view scanning mechanism to enhance detection precision through complementary contextual cues. However, we identify a previously overlooked structural deficiency in multi-view Mamba scanning for NTAD: redundancy accumulation. Specifically, distinct scanning branches capture substantial view-invariant information, which is repeatedly amplified during multi-view fusion; conversely, view-specific information is diluted or even suppressed, leading to representation homogenization and multi-view degradation. To address this problem, we propose DisenMamba, a novel disentangled multi-view Mamba framework. DisenMamba reformulates multi-view scanning as a two-stage disentangle-then-fuse process that explicitly separates view-invariant and view-specific components prior to fusion. This design prevents the invariant information accumulation while preserving complementary multi-view cues, yielding more discriminative representations for subtle traffic anomalies. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DisenMamba, establishing a new disentangled multi-view Mamba paradigm. Code is available at https://github.com/ikun0124/DisenMamba.

AI.tldr: DisenMamba is a novel disentangled multi-view Mamba framework for network traffic anomaly detection that addresses redundancy accumulation in multi-view scanning by separating view-invariant and view-specific components before fusion.
AI.motivation: While Mamba shows promise for NTAD with linear-time complexity and multi-view scanning, there's a previously overlooked structural deficiency: redundancy accumulation where view-invariant information is repeatedly amplified during multi-view fusion, while view-specific information gets diluted, leading to representation homogenization and multi-view degradation.
AI.method: DisenMamba reformulates multi-view scanning as a two-stage disentangle-then-fuse process that explicitly separates view-invariant and view-specific components prior to fusion. This prevents invariant information accumulation while preserving complementary multi-view cues.
AI.result: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of DisenMamba in yielding more discriminative representations for subtle traffic anomalies, establishing a new disentangled multi-view Mamba paradigm.
AI.conclusion: DisenMamba addresses the redundancy accumulation problem in multi-view Mamba scanning for NTAD, providing a more effective framework for traffic anomaly detection by preventing representation homogenization through explicit disentanglement of view-invariant and view-specific components.

title: Chamaileon: Cross-Context Binder Design with Contextualized Modeling and Mixed Sampling
summary: The rapid evolution of generative models has unlocked new potentials in protein binder design, a pivotal task in structural biology, by facilitating end-to-end generation via joint sequence-structure modeling or hallucination. However, existing approaches are predominantly implemented under a single-target, single-state assumption, limiting their ability to model multi-target or multi-state interactions required for advanced function-oriented protein design. Here, we introduce Chamaileon, which unifies multi-target and multi-state binder design by formulating the problem as cross-context binding landscape modeling. The framework is underpinned by a training paradigm termed In-Context Complex Co-Design (I3CD) for context-aware sequence-structure co-modeling. During inference, we employ Mixture-of-Paths Sampling (MoPS), a scalable strategy that optimizes a single sequence across contexts while alleviating the scarcity of high-quality multi-conformational paired data. Extensive evaluation on our newly constructed benchmark, CROSS, demonstrates that Chamaileon effectively generates sequences adaptable to diverse conformational landscapes and multi-target requirements. The code is available on https://github.com/caohengyuan/Chamaileon.

AI.tldr: Chamaileon is a novel framework for multi-target and multi-state protein binder design that uses cross-context binding landscape modeling with In-Context Complex Co-Design training and Mixture-of-Paths Sampling inference.
AI.motivation: Existing protein binder design approaches are limited by single-target, single-state assumptions, which prevents modeling of multi-target or multi-state interactions needed for advanced function-oriented protein design.
AI.method: The framework uses In-Context Complex Co-Design (I3CD) training for context-aware sequence-structure co-modeling, and Mixture-of-Paths Sampling (MoPS) inference strategy that optimizes single sequences across contexts while addressing the scarcity of multi-conformational paired data.
AI.result: Extensive evaluation on the newly constructed CROSS benchmark demonstrates that Chamaileon effectively generates sequences adaptable to diverse conformational landscapes and multi-target requirements.
AI.conclusion: Chamaileon successfully unifies multi-target and multi-state binder design by formulating the problem as cross-context binding landscape modeling, addressing limitations of existing approaches and advancing function-oriented protein design.

title: Coordinated Networking for On-Device Agent-Augmented Real-Time Communication
summary: AI agents are enabling a new paradigm of agent-augmented real-time communication (RTC), where humans focus on high-level collaboration, while agents autonomously retrieve, analyze, and generate information in real time to support their interactions. These apps enable new experiences across various domains: for example, when corporate employees co-author a legal document, their agents can discuss and draft on their behalf, sparing them the burden of manually reviewing each other's work. As existing cloud-based agents suffer from privacy risks and unscalable server costs, on-device agent-augmented RTC offers a promising alternative. However, this on-device paradigm introduces a new networking challenge: contention between concurrent traffic flows generated by humans (for live video streaming) and agents (for sending context files for analysis). We design HFS, a framework to ensure both high live video quality and low agent response latency in agent-augmented RTC apps. We achieve the goal through an app-guided multi-flow transport approach, where a unified app-layer orchestrator jointly controls the sending rates of live video and agent context flows based on their heterogeneous app requirements. Our prototype built atop WebRTC and llama.cpp demonstrates that HAFS outperforms baselines, achieving 1.5x higher video quality while reducing agent response time by 31%.

AI.tldr: HAFS is a framework for on-device agent-augmented real-time communication that optimizes network traffic between human video streams and agent context files to achieve both high video quality and low agent response latency.
AI.motivation: AI agents enable agent-augmented RTC where humans focus on high-level collaboration while agents handle information retrieval and analysis. While cloud-based agents have privacy risks and scalability issues, on-device alternatives introduce networking challenges due to contention between human video streams and agent context file transfers.
AI.method: HAFS uses an app-guided multi-flow transport approach with a unified app-layer orchestrator that jointly controls sending rates of live video and agent context flows based on their heterogeneous application requirements.
AI.result: The prototype built on WebRTC and llama.cpp shows HAFS achieves 1.5x higher video quality while reducing agent response time by 31% compared to baselines.
AI.conclusion: HAFS effectively addresses the networking challenges in on-device agent-augmented RTC by intelligently managing concurrent traffic flows, enabling both high-quality video communication and responsive agent support in real-time collaborative applications.

title: Neonatal Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy Classification from the EEG and HRV Signals Using a Conformer based Masked Autoencoder
comment: Paper submits to IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
summary: In this paper, we propose the MAEConformer, a novel self-supervised learning framework that combines the Conformer architecture with the Masked Autoencoder (MAE) paradigm for large-scale representation learning from unlabelled electroencephalography (EEG) and heart rate variability (HRV) signals. By integrating convolutional operations with Transformer-based self-attention, MAEConformer effectively captures both local temporal patterns and long-range contextual dependencies in physiological time series. To enhance reconstruction fidelity and representation quality, a multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform (MR-STFT) loss is incorporated alongside the reconstruction objective, enabling the model to jointly learn temporal and spectral characteristics across multiple scales. Modality-specific EEG and HRV MAEConformer models were pretrained on 6,030h and 4,868h of unlabelled recordings, respectively, and subsequently transferred to expert-annotated downstream tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the learned representations provide strong transferability and data efficiency. In EEG-based hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) severity classification, the pretrained MAE-EEG model achieved test AUCs of 97.19% and 96.56% for binary and four-class classification tasks, respectively, outperforming a range of state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised baselines. On the HRV-based HIE severity classification task, MAE-HRV achieved a test AUC of 82.42%, surpassing both self-supervised Transformer-based and supervised convolutional baselines. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of MAEConformer for learning robust and transferable representations across multiple physiological modalities.

AI.tldr: MAEConformer is a self-supervised learning framework that combines Conformer architecture with Masked Autoencoder paradigm for learning representations from EEG and HRV signals, achieving state-of-the-art performance on clinical classification tasks.
AI.motivation: To develop an effective self-supervised learning approach for large-scale representation learning from unlabelled physiological signals (EEG and HRV) that can capture both local temporal patterns and long-range dependencies, enabling robust transfer to downstream clinical tasks.
AI.method: Combines Conformer architecture (convolutional operations with Transformer self-attention) with Masked Autoencoder framework, incorporating multi-resolution short-time Fourier transform loss alongside reconstruction objective to learn temporal and spectral characteristics across multiple scales.
AI.result: Pretrained models achieved: 97.19% AUC for EEG-based binary HIE severity classification, 96.56% AUC for four-class classification, and 82.42% AUC for HRV-based HIE classification, outperforming state-of-the-art supervised and self-supervised baselines.
AI.conclusion: MAEConformer effectively learns robust and transferable representations from unlabelled physiological signals, demonstrating strong performance on downstream clinical classification tasks with data efficiency and transferability.

title: What Can Be Enforced? A Theory of Certified Runtime Safety for Tool-Using Agents
comment: 26 pages, 8 figures. Extended version with complete proofs and additional experiments
summary: Runtime guardrails act before irreversible tool calls, but their guarantees depend on what policy state is representable, what a judge observes, and whether intervention changes future behavior. We separate three questions. First, relative to fixed oracle predicates, a deterministic gate enforces exactly the nonempty safety policies whose good prefixes its register model recognizes; policy nontriviality is undecidable with two decrementable counters but in PSPACE for a separable monotone fragment. Second, under a fixed exogenous law, Neyman-Pearson gives the exact false-block/miss frontier and conformal calibration gives a finite-sample marginal certificate, possibly via block-all. Third, once blocking changes future proposals, static scores and ungated trajectories need not identify the closed-loop frontier; a specified finite controlled model instead yields an occupancy program. Bounded representation attacks add a robustness margin, so benign calibration alone does not transfer. Experiments target these distinctions through static diagnostics, controlled-model enumeration, representation rewrites, and paired closed-loop reruns.

AI.tldr: A theoretical analysis of runtime guardrails for AI systems, examining what safety policies are enforceable, how to make blocking decisions with statistical guarantees, and how blocking affects future behavior in closed-loop systems.
AI.motivation: Runtime guardrails are used to prevent unsafe tool calls in AI systems, but their effectiveness depends on policy representation, observation capabilities, and whether intervention changes future behavior. The paper aims to address the theoretical foundations and practical limitations of these safety mechanisms.
AI.method: Three-part theoretical framework: 1) Formal analysis of enforceable policies using register models and computability theory; 2) Statistical decision-making approaches (Neyman-Pearson, conformal calibration) for blocking decisions with fixed exogenous laws; 3) Analysis of closed-loop behavior when blocking affects future proposals, using occupancy programs and representation attacks.
AI.result: Found that: 1) Policy nontriviality is undecidable with two decrementable counters but in PSPACE for separable monotone fragments; 2) Neyman-Pearson provides exact false-block/miss frontiers while conformal calibration offers finite-sample marginal certificates; 3) Static scores and ungated trajectories don't identify closed-loop frontiers when blocking affects future behavior, requiring controlled model enumeration instead.
AI.conclusion: Runtime guardrails require careful theoretical foundations: different aspects (policy representability, statistical guarantees, closed-loop effects) demand distinct analytical approaches. Benign calibration alone doesn't guarantee robustness to representation attacks, highlighting the need for comprehensive theoretical frameworks and experimental validation of these distinctions.

title: Random Forest-Based Prediction of Bone Volume Fraction and Fracture Position from S-Parameters
comment: 5 pages,6 figures,This is a summary report prepared by undergraduate students I supervised, formatted as a letter
summary: In this paper, we propose a method for predicting bone volume fraction (BVF) and fracture position by constructing a random forest model based on multichannel S-parameters. A nine-antenna microwave scanning system is designed and fabricated to acquire the multichannel S-parameter data. Bone-mimicking phantoms are developed, and corresponding experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. Both synthetic and experimental results demonstrate the validity of the method.

AI.tldr: A random forest model uses multichannel S-parameters from a nine-antenna microwave system to predict bone volume fraction and fracture positions, validated with bone-mimicking phantoms.
AI.motivation: There's a need for non-invasive methods to assess bone health and predict fracture risks. The paper aims to develop a microwave-based approach for predicting bone volume fraction and identifying potential fracture positions, which could be valuable for osteoporosis diagnosis and fracture prevention.
AI.method: The researchers constructed a random forest model using multichannel S-parameters. They designed and fabricated a nine-antenna microwave scanning system to acquire the data, and developed bone-mimicking phantoms for experimental validation. The approach combines microwave sensing with machine learning for bone assessment.
AI.result: Both synthetic and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective for predicting bone volume fraction and fracture positions. The microwave system successfully acquired multichannel S-parameter data, and the random forest model made accurate predictions using this data.
AI.conclusion: The proposed microwave-based approach using a random forest model with multichannel S-parameters is a valid method for non-invasive bone assessment. It shows promise for predicting bone volume fraction and identifying fracture positions, potentially offering a new tool for bone health monitoring and fracture risk assessment.

title: Physical AI Governance: From Theory to Practice Across Life Cycle
summary: With the emergence of Physical AI, artificial intelligence is extending beyond screen-based applications to embodied systems that perceive, interact with, and act in the physical world. Unlike traditional AI, Physical AI operates under real-time safety constraints, continuously interacts with dynamic environments, and coexists with humans, introducing governance challenges that existing AI governance frameworks do not explicitly address. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of Physical AI governance from both scientific and operational perspectives. We synthesize existing governance principles and organize them into a unified governance framework tailored to physical AI systems. Building on this foundation, we propose a five-stage Physical AI lifecycle comprising research, design, data, model development, and deployment, and demonstrate how governance can be operationalized across each stage through concrete implementation practices. By connecting governance principles with engineering workflows, this survey provides a structured reference for researchers, developers, and policymakers to build Physical AI systems that are safe, trustworthy, and aligned with societal values.

AI.tldr: A comprehensive survey proposing governance framework and lifecycle for Physical AI systems that operate in physical environments with real-time safety constraints.
AI.motivation: Physical AI extends beyond screen-based applications to embodied systems that interact with the physical world, posing new governance challenges that existing AI frameworks don't address due to real-time safety constraints, continuous interaction with dynamic environments, and human coexistence.
AI.method: Conducts a comprehensive survey of Physical AI governance, synthesizes existing principles into a unified governance framework, and proposes a five-stage Physical AI lifecycle (research, design, data, model development, deployment) with concrete implementation practices for each stage.
AI.result: Provides a structured governance framework tailored to Physical AI systems that connects governance principles with engineering workflows, enabling operationalization of governance across the entire Physical AI lifecycle.
AI.conclusion: The survey offers a practical reference for researchers, developers, and policymakers to build Physical AI systems that are safe, trustworthy, and aligned with societal values by integrating governance into all stages of development and deployment.

title: MS-GPT: Rethinking MS/MS De Novo Structure Elucidation as Spectrum-Induced Posterior Querying of a Molecule-Language Model
comment: 18 pages, 14 figures, and 9 tables, including appendices. Source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT
summary: Molecular structure elucidation from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) is a central inverse problem in analytical chemistry. Most existing approaches to MS/MS identification remain tied to reference libraries or predefined candidate sets, whereas de novo methods aim to generate structures directly from spectra. A common de novo route predicts a molecular fingerprint from the spectrum and then decodes structures from it, enabling decoder pretraining on large molecule-only corpora. However, this paradigm creates a training-inference mismatch: the decoder is trained on oracle fingerprints computed from molecules, but at inference it is queried with a noisy spectrum-induced fingerprint posterior that is typically collapsed to a single thresholded fingerprint. We introduce MS-GPT, which recasts fingerprint-mediated de novo elucidation as spectrum-induced posterior querying of a conditional molecule-language model. MS-GPT conditions a molecule-language model on fingerprints and formulas, then converts the spectrum-induced posterior into a band of fingerprint queries near the oracle-fingerprint manifold through active-bit density calibration. Candidates sampled across this band are pooled and ranked by generation-frequency consensus. A lightweight LoRA adapter further mitigates domain-specific posterior bias while preserving the pretrained molecular prior. On NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym, MS-GPT sets a new state of the art, reaching Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy of 29.8\%/41.1\% and 23.9\%/28.7\%, respectively. Candidate-pool scaling shows that efficient autoregressive molecular generation continues to improve recall with a little additional inference cost. The source code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/VIKI623/MS-GPT.

AI.tldr: MS-GPT introduces a new approach for molecular structure elucidation from mass spectra that reformulates fingerprint-mediated de novo methods as spectrum-induced posterior querying of a conditional molecule-language model, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy.
AI.motivation: Existing MS/MS identification methods rely on reference libraries or predefined candidate sets, while de novo methods face a training-inference mismatch where decoders are trained on clean oracle fingerprints but must work with noisy spectrum-induced fingerprint posteriors at inference time.
AI.method: MS-GPT recasts the problem as spectrum-induced posterior querying of a conditional molecule-language model. It conditions a molecule-language model on fingerprints and formulas, converts the spectrum-induced posterior into a band of fingerprint queries near the oracle-fingerprint manifold via active-bit density calibration, pools candidates sampled across this band, and ranks them by generation-frequency consensus. A lightweight LoRA adapter mitigates domain-specific posterior bias.
AI.result: On NPLIB1 and MassSpecGym datasets, MS-GPT achieves state-of-the-art performance with Top-1/Top-10 exact-match accuracy of 29.8%/41.1% and 23.9%/28.7% respectively. Candidate-pool scaling shows that efficient autoregressive molecular generation continues to improve recall with minimal additional inference cost.
AI.conclusion: MS-GPT successfully addresses the training-inference mismatch in de novo molecular structure elucidation by treating it as a posterior querying problem, outperforming existing methods while maintaining computational efficiency through autoregressive generation and smart candidate pooling strategies.

title: How Well Can AI Generate Backlogs from App Mockups?
comment: Accepted at the AIRE Workshop, IEEE 34th International Requirements Engineering Conference (RE) 2026
summary: Creating sprint backlogs requires considerable effort, as items such as epics, user stories, and tasks can be missed or inconsistently specified. We propose a multimodal approach to support backlog generation from visual app mockups, an artifact available at early project stages. We evaluate three prompting strategies on GPT-4o: a zero-shot baseline, Compositional Chain-of-Thought (CCoT) for vision-language reasoning, and a persona-driven prompt. We study seven app development projects across two countries and interview developers about the results. Overall, we observed that the baseline prompt favours recall over precision, whereas CCoT is more balanced, achieving average F1 scores of 52-66% for epics and user stories. Tasks were more challenging to generate accurately. Precision gains were most consistent when adding architectural context, particularly for backend tasks (precision gains up to 35%). Interviews with developers revealed that up to 26% of false positives were still considered useful, reflecting the creative and open-ended nature of backlog creation. To capture this, we propose a new measure called Revised Recall, which complements ground-truth evaluation with developer assessments. Our findings suggest that hybrid prompting with architectural context can assist backlog generation from early mockups, though results vary by item type and developer oversight remains necessary.

AI.tldr: A multimodal approach using GPT-4o with three prompting strategies (zero-shot baseline, Compositional Chain-of-Thought, persona-driven) generates sprint backlogs from visual app mockups, achieving best results with CCoT for balanced F1 scores (52-66%) for epics/user stories.
AI.motivation: Creating sprint backlogs requires considerable effort and items like epics, user stories, and tasks are often missed or inconsistently specified. Early project artifacts like visual app mockups could serve as input for automated backlog generation to reduce manual effort.
AI.method: Proposed multimodal approach using GPT-4o with three prompting strategies: 1) zero-shot baseline, 2) Compositional Chain-of-Thought for vision-language reasoning, and 3) persona-driven prompt. Evaluated on seven app development projects across two countries with developer interviews about results.
AI.result: Baseline prompt favors recall over precision, while CCoT is more balanced with average F1 scores of 52-66% for epics and user stories. Tasks were more challenging. Precision gains were most consistent when adding architectural context (up to 35% for backend tasks). Developers found up to 26% of false positives useful, leading to proposal of "Revised Recall" metric that complements ground-truth evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Hybrid prompting with architectural context can assist backlog generation from early mockups, though results vary by item type and developer oversight remains necessary. The proposed Revised Recall metric better captures the creative nature of backlog creation.

title: Restoration Flow Matching-Based Channel Refinement and Equalization Correction for MIMO Semantic Communications
summary: In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) semantic communication, imperfect channel state information (CSI) and equalization mismatch can seriously degrade semantic reconstruction quality. To address this issue, we propose a unified restoration flow matching (RFM)-based framework for channel refinement and equalization correction. Specifically, the channel RFM (CRFM) module is developed to refine the coarse channel, thereby improving channel estimation accuracy. Based on the refined channel, the developed semantic RFM (SRFM) module is employed to correct the residual distortions in the post-equalization latent space. The key idea is to formulate the two cascaded inverse problems of channel estimation and equalization as the unified conditional restoration task, in which the learned conditional velocity field guides the perturbed distribution towards the target distribution. To enhance the robustness of these two modules under various distortion conditions, we develop a dual-anchor perturbation training strategy that jointly learns near-manifold refinement and large-error correction, and implement inference through a few-step deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) solver. Extensive experiments on MIMO channels and visual semantic transmission tasks demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves key metrics for channel estimation and semantic reconstruction quality. Moreover, compared with representative diffusion-based generative baselines, the proposed method requires fewer sampling steps.

AI.tldr: A unified RFM-based framework that addresses channel estimation and equalization issues in MIMO semantic communication through conditional restoration, improving both channel accuracy and semantic reconstruction quality with fewer sampling steps than diffusion-based methods.
AI.motivation: Imperfect channel state information (CSI) and equalization mismatch in MIMO semantic communication seriously degrade semantic reconstruction quality. Traditional approaches struggle with these cascaded inverse problems, creating a need for a unified framework that can handle both channel refinement and equalization correction.
AI.method: Proposes a unified restoration flow matching (RFM)-based framework with two modules: 1) Channel RFM (CRFM) refines coarse channel estimates to improve accuracy, and 2) Semantic RFM (SRFM) corrects residual distortions in post-equalization latent space. Uses a conditional restoration task formulation where learned conditional velocity fields guide perturbed distributions toward target distributions. Implements dual-anchor perturbation training strategy for robustness under various distortion conditions, and uses few-step deterministic ODE solver for inference.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on MIMO channels and visual semantic transmission tasks demonstrate improvements in key metrics for both channel estimation and semantic reconstruction quality. The method requires fewer sampling steps compared to representative diffusion-based generative baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed RFM-based framework effectively addresses the joint challenges of channel estimation and equalization correction in MIMO semantic communication, offering improved performance with computational efficiency through fewer sampling steps, making it a practical solution for real-world deployment.

title: Optimal Reward Shaping: Autonomous Car Parking Case Study
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures. Includes supplementary video demonstration and open-source code link
summary: Designing effective reward functions for model-free reinforcement learning under non-holonomic constraints remains a persistent challenge, often resulting in severe local minima such as policy paralysis or over-conservative hazard avoidance. In this work, we present a parameterized reward shaping framework featuring coverage-gated alignment feedback, drive-direction switch regularization, and an aligned episode termination mechanism evaluated on an autonomous parallel parking task. Crucially, we show that environmental reward parameters and algorithmic hyperparameters are deeply co-dependent, requiring joint meta-optimization to achieve stable convergence. By employing surrogate-based Bayesian optimization, our co-optimized Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent resolves characteristic control failure modes, significantly outperforming uncalibrated baselines across both success rate and trajectory smoothness.

AI.tldr: A reward shaping framework with coverage-gated alignment feedback, drive-direction regularization, and aligned termination for autonomous parallel parking under non-holonomic constraints, requiring joint meta-optimization of reward and algorithm parameters via Bayesian optimization to overcome local minima.
AI.motivation: Designing effective reward functions for model-free reinforcement learning under non-holonomic constraints is challenging, often leading to severe local minima like policy paralysis or over-conservative hazard avoidance in tasks like autonomous parallel parking.
AI.method: Developed a parameterized reward shaping framework with three key components: coverage-gated alignment feedback, drive-direction switch regularization, and aligned episode termination mechanism. Employed surrogate-based Bayesian optimization for joint meta-optimization of environmental reward parameters and algorithmic hyperparameters, which were found to be deeply co-dependent.
AI.result: The co-optimized Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent successfully resolved characteristic control failure modes, significantly outperforming uncalibrated baselines in both success rate and trajectory smoothness on autonomous parallel parking tasks.
AI.conclusion: Joint meta-optimization of reward parameters and algorithmic hyperparameters through Bayesian optimization is crucial for stable convergence in model-free RL under non-holonomic constraints, enabling effective autonomous parallel parking through carefully designed reward shaping.

title: SAGE: Safety-First Defense-in-Depth Guardrails for Verified Lifecycle Control of High-Impact Generative AI
summary:
High-impact generative AI makes catastrophic misuse a lifecycle-control problem, not merely a prompt-filtering problem. SAGE is a safety-first, authorization-separated architecture in which credible catastrophic-enablement risk constrains admissibility before utility, latency, or commercial objectives are considered. It combines signed release manifests, diverse detectors, robust risk envelopes, least-risk defaults, output checking, three-valued monitoring, protected audit chains, containment, and rollback. Formal results establish safety priority, conservative detector bounds, monotone release gating, tamper-evident records, and an authorization cut; two PRISM abstractions verify authorization separation and lifecycle invariants under explicit assumptions.
  A frozen, vendor-symmetric study sent 84 cases to each of four GPT, four Claude, and two Gemini snapshots: 840 calls yielded 794 target responses, 46 provider errors, and 449 successful judgments covering 375 responses. Eight snapshots had complete judged domain coverage. Harmful-compliance estimates were low; variation arose mainly from benign utility and safe redirection. Seven multiplicity-adjusted contrasts involving Claude, Gemini, or GPT-5 snapshots and the GPT-5 mini and GPT-5 nano snapshots were supported, while no tested contrast between the Claude or Gemini snapshots and GPT-5 or GPT-5.5 survived correction.
  The observed harmful-compliance range is a conservative, protocol-bound view from one generation per prompt with no tools, retrieval, history, or human adjudication; it is not an upper bound on operational assistance. A preregistered extension specifies how to test a wider best-worst gap using a locked split, repeated sampling, multi-turn and sandboxed-tool conditions, and domain-expert scoring.

AI.tldr: SAGE is a safety-first AI architecture prioritizing catastrophic risk prevention over utility, with formal verification and empirical testing showing low harmful compliance in current models.
AI.motivation: High-impact generative AI requires addressing catastrophic misuse as a lifecycle control problem, not just prompt filtering, necessitating architectures that prioritize safety before utility considerations.
AI.method: SAGE architecture combines signed release manifests, diverse detectors, risk envelopes, least-risk defaults, output checking, monitoring, protected audit chains, containment, and rollback with formal verification of safety properties.
AI.result: Empirical study of 840 API calls across 10 model snapshots showed low harmful-compliance estimates with variation mainly from benign utility differences; 7 of 8 tested model contrasts showed statistically significant differences but not between Claude/Gemini and GPT-5 variants.
AI.conclusion: Catastrophic AI misuse requires lifecycle control solutions like SAGE; current models show low harmful compliance but observed ranges are conservative protocol-bound estimates that don't represent operational upper bounds.

title: Variational-Ising-Attention (VIA):TailoredAttentionMattersfor Science
summary: Attention enables context modeling via query-key scoring with softmax normalization. Driven by industrial long-context demands, mainstream research has converged toward sparsity and efficiency--yet softmax's independence assumption persists. For scientific tasks unburdened by long-token constraints, however, richer structured coupling may often be essential, making tailored attention both viable and more appropriate. To this end, we propose Variational-Ising-Attention (VIA), which augments softmax normalization with an interacting Ising model; attention patterns emerge from learnable pairwise couplings via variational mean-field inference, redefining attention from a ranking over isolated items to a collective state over interacting entities. We instantiate VIA on retrosynthesis reaction center prediction, a task inherently governed by cooperative bond-breaking constraints. Comprehensive experiments across model variants, coupled with mechanistic analyses, demonstrate that VIA consistently and substantially outperforms standard softmax attention. More broadly, our findings suggest that for scientific problems, the optimal solution is not general-purpose efficiency, but appropriately tailored attention aligned with intrinsic domain structure. This work provides a theoretically grounded and empirically validated instantiation of this paradigm.

AI.tldr: VIA (Variational-Ising-Attention) replaces standard softmax attention with an Ising model that learns pairwise couplings between attention elements, enabling structured context modeling for scientific tasks where cooperative constraints are essential.
AI.motivation: Current attention mechanisms rely on softmax normalization with independence assumptions, optimized for industrial long-context efficiency via sparsity. However, scientific tasks often require richer structured coupling that standard attention cannot capture, making tailored attention mechanisms both viable and necessary for these domains.
AI.method: VIA augments standard softmax attention with an interacting Ising model. Instead of treating attention scores as independent, it learns pairwise couplings between elements and uses variational mean-field inference to derive attention patterns, transforming attention from a ranking over isolated items to a collective state over interacting entities.
AI.result: VIA substantially outperforms standard softmax attention on retrosynthesis reaction center prediction, a task governed by cooperative bond-breaking constraints. Comprehensive experiments across model variants and mechanistic analyses demonstrate consistent performance improvements.
AI.conclusion: For scientific problems, the optimal solution is not general-purpose efficient attention, but appropriately tailored attention aligned with intrinsic domain structure. VIA provides a theoretically grounded instantiation of this paradigm that redefines attention as a collective state over interacting entities rather than independent rankings.

title: Design Theater: A Benchmark for Generative UI
summary: Generative UI tools promise to democratize UI design by turning natural language descriptions into complete interfaces. Alongside the interface, these tools generate user-facing design rationales that explain their layout, accessibility, and design choices. However, it remains unclear whether these stated rationales are actually reflected in the interfaces they produce. We call this disconnect ``Design Theater'': plausible and confident design rationales that have little relationship to the actual implementation. To study this phenomenon, we introduce a benchmark and three metrics for measuring Design Theater. The benchmark includes 24 UI generation tasks spanning structural, styling, and functional design requirements. Using this benchmark, we evaluate 120 interfaces created by five generative UI tools. On average, over 25\% of user-facing design rationales are not implemented in the generated interface, and the implementation failure increases to 34\% for functional requirements. Tools recognize roughly half of the UX principles embedded in prompts (mean = 0.54), with four of five tools implementing 6\% or fewer functional principles. We also measure interface similarity across tools and find convergence in visual appearance and layout organization, with greater variation in color choices. Overall, we contribute: 1) the concept of Design Theater; 2) a benchmark with metrics for assessing whether the stated reasoning of generative UI tools is reflected in their implementations; 3) and findings from a systematic evaluation of these tools. We discuss what these findings mean for the design and evaluation of generative UI tools.

AI.tldr: Generative UI tools often produce "Design Theater" - confident design rationales that don't match their actual interface implementations, with 25-34% of rationales not implemented and poor recognition of functional requirements.
AI.motivation: While generative UI tools promise to democratize UI design by creating interfaces from natural language descriptions and providing user-facing design rationales, there's a concern about whether these stated rationales actually correspond to the generated interfaces.
AI.method: The authors introduce a benchmark with 24 UI generation tasks covering structural, styling, and functional requirements. They evaluate 120 interfaces from five generative UI tools, measuring Design Theater through three metrics to assess implementation-reasoning disconnect.
AI.result: Over 25% of design rationales are not implemented in generated interfaces (rising to 34% for functional requirements). Tools only recognize about half of UX principles in prompts (mean = 0.54), with four of five tools implementing 6% or fewer functional principles. Interface similarity shows convergence in visual appearance and layout, but variation in color.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals significant "Design Theater" in generative UI tools, highlighting a disconnect between stated rationales and actual implementations. This has important implications for designing and evaluating generative UI tools to ensure they deliver on their promises rather than producing superficial justifications.

title: CALMRec: Causally Aligned Language Memory for Long-Horizon Recommendation
summary: Large language models (LLMs) can summarize heterogeneous user evidence in natural language, but current LLM recommenders often collapse enduring preferences, transient intent, and exposure-induced behavior into one profile. This makes recommendation vulnerable to feedback loops: repeated exposure is mistaken for preference, immediate clicks dominate delayed satisfaction, and fluent explanations need not reflect the ranking decision. We propose our method, a model-agnostic framework for long-horizon recommendation. Our method uses a frozen multimodal language model to convert item content and feedback into evidence-grounded semantic atoms, then maintains separate short-term, long-term, and exposure memories. Propensity-weighted updates reduce policy-induced exposure bias, while a conservative offline critic reranks candidates for delayed satisfaction under a behavior-support constraint. Explanations use only influential evidence atoms and are checked by counterfactual deletion. We provide an identification result and evaluate the framework in e-commerce-like, news-like, and short-video-like environments. Across ten seeds, our method improves discounted long-term value over the strongest alternative by 6.1%, 7.6%, and 6.7%, respectively. Twenty-seed paired ablations show significant value drops after removing propensity correction (0.739 +/- 0.191) or conservative support regularization (0.523 +/- 0.234). A frozen instruction language model also more than doubles semantic-atom NDCG over TF-IDF on a held-out paraphrase benchmark.

AI.tldr: A model-agnostic framework for long-horizon recommendation that separates user preferences from transient behaviors using semantic atoms and multiple memory types to prevent feedback loops and improve delayed satisfaction.
AI.motivation: Current LLM-based recommenders conflate enduring preferences, transient intent, and exposure-induced behavior into a single profile, creating feedback loops where repeated exposure is mistaken for preference and immediate clicks dominate delayed satisfaction. Fluent explanations from LLMs don't necessarily reflect actual ranking decisions.
AI.method: Uses a frozen multimodal language model to convert item content and feedback into evidence-grounded semantic atoms. Maintains separate short-term, long-term, and exposure memories. Employs propensity-weighted updates to reduce policy-induced exposure bias, and uses a conservative offline critic to rerank candidates for delayed satisfaction with behavior-support constraints. Explanations use only influential evidence atoms and are validated by counterfactual deletion.
AI.result: In e-commerce-like, news-like, and short-video-like environments across ten seeds, the method improved discounted long-term value over the strongest alternative by 6.1%, 7.6%, and 6.7% respectively. Ablations showed significant value drops when removing propensity correction (0.739 +/- 0.191) or conservative support regularization (0.523 +/- 0.234). The frozen instruction language model more than doubled semantic-atom NDCG over TF-IDF on a held-out paraphrase benchmark.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully addresses feedback loops in LLM-based recommendation by separating different types of user evidence, reducing exposure bias, and optimizing for long-term satisfaction while providing reliable explanations, demonstrating significant improvements over alternatives across multiple recommendation scenarios.

title: DP-IVON-Gradsq: Differentially Private Squared-Gradient Improved Variational Online Newton
comment: Accepted at the 2nd Workshop on Machine Unlearning and Privacy Preservation (WIPE-OUT 2), held in conjunction with ECML PKDD 2026
summary: Differential privacy provides formal privacy guarantees for training neural networks on sensitive data, while Bayesian deep learning offers a principled framework for uncertainty-aware prediction. Combining these two objectives remains challenging, as privacy noise can interact with the stochasticity introduced by Bayesian posterior sampling. In this work, we investigate differentially private variational Bayesian learning through the Improved Variational Online Newton (IVON) optimizer. We introduce DP-IVON-Gradsq, a private variant of IVON. The proposed method constructs its curvature estimate from the privatized gradient using a noise-corrected squared-gradient estimator, reducing the direct interaction between posterior-sampling noise and privacy noise while preserving the Adam-like computational efficiency of IVON. We evaluate DP-IVON-Gradsq on CIFAR-10 against the standard private optimizers DP-SGD and DP-Adam over a range of privacy budgets. The results show that DP-IVON-Gradsq is competitive under weak-to-moderate privacy constraints, i.e., large-to-moderate values of $\varepsilon$, while degrading under strong privacy. Code is available at https://github.com/NourJamoussi/DP-IVON-Gradsq.git.

AI.tldr: A method called DP-IVON-Gradsq combines differential privacy with Bayesian deep learning by adapting the IVON optimizer, using noise-corrected squared-gradient estimators to manage privacy noise while maintaining computational efficiency.
AI.motivation: Differential privacy provides formal privacy guarantees for neural networks on sensitive data, and Bayesian deep learning offers uncertainty-aware prediction. Combining these two objectives is challenging because privacy noise interacts with the stochasticity from Bayesian posterior sampling.
AI.method: The proposed method DP-IVON-Gradsq adapts the Improved Variational Online Newton (IVON) optimizer. It constructs curvature estimates from privatized gradients using a noise-corrected squared-gradient estimator, reducing the interaction between posterior-sampling noise and privacy noise while preserving Adam-like computational efficiency.
AI.result: DP-IVON-Gradsq was evaluated on CIFAR-10 against standard private optimizers DP-SGD and DP-Adam across various privacy budgets. The method is competitive under weak-to-moderate privacy constraints (large-to-moderate ε values) but degrades under strong privacy constraints.
AI.conclusion: DP-IVON-Gradsq successfully combines differential privacy with Bayesian variational learning, offering a practical solution for privacy-preserving uncertainty-aware deep learning that works well for moderate privacy requirements but faces challenges under very strict privacy constraints.

title: Share No More Than the Request Requires: Federated Disclosure for Perspective-Aware AI
summary: Modern AI systems bring societal risks such as mass surveillance, extreme concentrations of power, and loss of user autonomy---calling into question a model where third-parties collect and control massive amounts of user data. Users require a sovereign system to securely own, govern, and disclose their context while remaining compliant across regulated domains with strict provenance, interpretability, and policy adherence. Perspective-aware AI approaches this by transforming a user's aggregated personal data into a structured identity model called a \emph{Chronicle}: a temporal knowledge graph that represents and grows with the user. Chronicles support the secure disclosure of context across federated networks. A Chronicle holder may expose a queryable, authorized view that a third-party agent may consult without centralizing anyone's data. This paper explores the problem of minimum-necessary disclosure across domain boundaries: when a requester's agent queries a Chronicle, how can the system constrain its response to release only what the requester's relationship, stated purpose, and specific task require? We propose \textbf{Provenance Preserving Chronicles} (PPC), a federated protocol that compiles each holder's Chronicle into a compact \emph{authorized evidence subgraph} governed by one rule: \emph{share no more than the request requires}. Holders keep local sovereignty; an access controller projects relationship-aware views over domain-expert ontologies; and a two-phase flow returns provenance-linked text first, releasing raw artifacts only after explicit holder approval. We frame the problem, map gaps in blockchain, P2P, and holder-sovereign designs, define the core constructs, and sketch the protocol with an explicit threat model.

AI.tldr: A sovereign AI system called Provenance Preserving Chronicles enables users to securely control and disclose only necessary personal data via temporal knowledge graphs, preventing over-sharing to third parties while maintaining compliance and provenance.
AI.motivation: Modern AI systems create risks like mass surveillance, power concentration, and loss of user autonomy from third-party data collection. Users need sovereign systems to own, govern, and disclose personal context securely while remaining compliant with strict provenance, interpretability, and policy requirements across regulated domains.
AI.method: Perspective-aware AI transforms personal data into structured identity models called Chronicles (temporal knowledge graphs). The paper proposes Provenance Preserving Chronicles (PPC), a federated protocol that compiles Chronicles into authorized evidence subgraphs governed by "share no more than the request requires." It uses an access controller for relationship-aware views over domain ontologies with a two-phase flow: returning provenance-linked text first, then raw artifacts only after explicit holder approval.
AI.result: The paper frames the problem of minimum-necessary disclosure across domain boundaries, maps gaps in existing designs (blockchain, P2P, holder-sovereign), defines core constructs, sketches the PPC protocol with explicit threat model, and proposes a system where holders maintain local sovereignty while enabling constrained data disclosure.
AI.conclusion: Provenance Preserving Chronicles offer a practical approach to sovereign data governance by enabling users to securely disclose only what is necessary for specific requests, addressing privacy risks while maintaining compliance and provenance requirements in regulated domains.

title: Breaking the Total Variance Barrier: Sharp Sample Complexity for Linear Heteroscedastic Bandits with Fixed Action Set
summary: Recent years have witnessed increasing interests in tackling heteroscedastic noise in bandits and reinforcement learning. In these works, the cumulative variance of the noise $Λ= \sum_{t=1}^T σ_t^2$, where $σ_t^2$ is the variance of the noise at round $t$, is used to characterize the statistical complexity of the problem, yielding \emph{simple regret} bounds of order $\tilde{\cal{O}}(d \sqrt{Λ/ T^2})$ for $d$-dimensional linear bandits with heteroscedastic noise. However, with a closer look, $Λ$ remains the same order even if the noise is close to zero at half of the rounds, which indicates that the $Λ$-dependence is not optimal. In this paper, we revisit the stochastic linear bandit problem with heteroscedastic noise, where the action set is prefixed throughout the learning process. We propose a novel variance-adaptive algorithm \texttt{VAEE} (Variance-Aware Exploration with Elimination) for large action set, which actively explores actions that maximizes the information gain among a candidate set of actions that are not eliminated. With the active-exploration strategy, we show that \texttt{VAEE} achieves a \emph{simple regret} with a nearly \emph{harmonic-mean} dependent rate. For finitely many actions, we propose a variance-aware variant of G-optimal design based exploration, which achieves a simple regret with sharper dependence on $d$. We also establish a nearly matching lower bound for the fixed action set setting indicating that \emph{harmonic-mean} dependent rate is unavoidable. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work that breaks the $\sqrtΛ$ barrier for stochastic linear bandits with heteroscedastic noise.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces novel variance-adaptive algorithms for stochastic linear bandits with heteroscedastic noise, achieving improved regret bounds that break the traditional $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ barrier by using harmonic-mean dependence instead.
AI.motivation: Existing work on heteroscedastic noise in bandits uses cumulative variance $\Lambda$ to characterize complexity, but this metric is suboptimal because $\Lambda$ remains the same order even when noise is near zero for many rounds. The $\Lambda$-dependence fails to capture the actual statistical complexity accurately.
AI.method: For large action sets: Proposed VAEE (Variance-Aware Exploration with Elimination) which actively explores actions maximizing information gain among non-eliminated candidates. For finite action sets: Developed a variance-aware variant of G-optimal design based exploration for sharper dimension dependence.
AI.result: VAEE achieves simple regret with nearly harmonic-mean dependent rate, breaking the $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ barrier. Established nearly matching lower bounds showing harmonic-mean dependence is unavoidable for fixed action sets. This represents the first work to overcome the $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ limitation for stochastic linear bandits with heteroscedastic noise.
AI.conclusion: Harmonic-mean dependence provides a more refined characterization of statistical complexity for heteroscedastic noise in linear bandits, with both algorithmic upper bounds and theoretical lower bounds demonstrating its optimality over traditional $\sqrt{\Lambda}$ dependence.

title: ConsistencyGate: Preventing Memory Contamination in LLM Agents via Self-Consistency Admission Control
comment: 24 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables, 1 algorithm; includes appendices
summary: LLM agents that operate over many turns accumulate facts in an external memory store and reuse them as premises for downstream reasoning. A hallucinated fact written at one step therefore persists as a false premise for every subsequent step, a failure mode we call memory contamination. Existing memory management addresses retrieval and capacity but not write-time correctness; this admission problem cannot be solved by utility- or recency-based criteria, and uncontrolled contamination compounds across long trajectories. We propose ConsistencyGate, a write-time admission gate that, before committing a candidate fact m extracted from context c, queries the LLM K times for a soft support score and admits m only when the average exceeds a threshold. The mechanism is model-agnostic, requires no fine-tuning, and reduces to a single forward pass in a log-probability variant for latency-sensitive deployments. To measure the effect on natural data, we construct two real-conversation benchmarks (LoCoMo-Contam and MSC-Contam) by planting controlled single-detail corruptions in long-term conversations from LoCoMo and MSC, and complement them with a structured synthetic corpus (MemContam) that isolates a near-oracle upper bound. Across four LLM backbones, ConsistencyGate reduces contamination on every benchmark relative to a write-everything baseline, with the cost concentrated on facts that are stated only implicitly in the source context. We release all three benchmarks together with the gate implementation.

AI.tldr: ConsistencyGate is a write-time admission mechanism that prevents hallucinated facts from contaminating LLM agent memory by verifying candidate facts through multiple queries before committing them to memory.
AI.motivation: LLM agents that accumulate facts in external memory face "memory contamination" where a single hallucinated fact becomes a persistent false premise for all subsequent reasoning. Existing memory management focuses on retrieval and capacity but doesn't address write-time correctness.
AI.method: ConsistencyGate queries the LLM K times to get a soft support score for candidate facts before committing them to memory, only admitting facts when average support exceeds a threshold. The method is model-agnostic, requires no fine-tuning, and has a log-probability variant for latency-sensitive deployments.
AI.result: Across four LLM backbones, ConsistencyGate reduces contamination on all three benchmarks (LoCoMo-Contam, MSC-Contam, and synthetic MemContam) relative to a write-everything baseline, though with cost concentrated on implicitly stated facts.
AI.conclusion: Write-time admission through consistency checking effectively reduces memory contamination in LLM agents, with benchmarks and implementation released to the community.

title: Extreme Volatility Warning under Label Scarcity via Multi-Source Anomaly Fusion
summary: Early warning of extreme market volatility is central to financial risk management, but actionable events are rare, nonstationary, and often triggered by exogenous information shocks. In our CSI~300 setting, only $\sim$80 positive samples are observed across 791 training days, making heavily supervised multi-source models unstable. We first analyze a 100K-parameter hierarchical text-signal fusion model (HTSF) and find that added parameterization hurts in this low-label regime. Motivated by this failure, we propose \textbf{AAMSF} (Anomaly-Augmented Multi-Signal Fusion), a semisupervised framework that combines Isolation Forest anomaly scores over market indicators, GDELT events, Chinese financial news, and English media with lightweight Ridge score fusion. We further introduce \textbf{T-AAMSF}, a temporal extension for multi-day anomaly accumulation. On CSI~300 (2018--2023), AAMSF achieves test AUC-ROC \textbf{0.680}, outperforming the strongest unsupervised baseline (0.630) and neural baseline (0.588), while T-AAMSF improves PR-AUC to 0.291. Ablations reveal strong source asymmetry: GDELT and domestic financial news provide complementary risk signals, whereas English media consistently reduces performance, and learned weighting is unreliable under validation noise. These results suggest an empirical design principle for label-scarce financial risk warning: robust anomaly geometry and source reliability can matter more than supervised representation capacity.

AI.tldr: A semi-supervised anomaly detection framework (AAMSF) for early warning of extreme market volatility that combines anomaly scores from multiple data sources using lightweight fusion, outperforming neural baselines in low-label regimes.
AI.motivation: Early warning of extreme market volatility is crucial for financial risk management, but actionable events are rare, nonstationary, and triggered by exogenous information shocks. In the CSI~300 setting, only about 80 positive samples exist across 791 training days, making heavily supervised multi-source models unstable.
AI.method: Proposed AAMSF (Anomaly-Augmented Multi-Signal Fusion), a semi-supervised framework that combines Isolation Forest anomaly scores over market indicators, GDELT events, Chinese financial news, and English media with lightweight Ridge score fusion. Also introduced T-AAMSF, a temporal extension for multi-day anomaly accumulation.
AI.result: On CSI~300 (2018-2023), AAMSF achieves test AUC-ROC of 0.680, outperforming strongest unsupervised baseline (0.630) and neural baseline (0.588). T-AAMSF improves PR-AUC to 0.291. Ablations show strong source asymmetry: GDELT and domestic financial news provide complementary risk signals, while English media reduces performance, and learned weighting is unreliable under validation noise.
AI.conclusion: For label-scarce financial risk warning, robust anomaly geometry and source reliability matter more than supervised representation capacity, suggesting an empirical design principle favoring simple but reliable anomaly detection over complex neural architectures in low-data regimes.

title: Reason Popper-ly: Patching In-Context Reasoning with Inductive Logic Programming
comment: Accepted at the 20th Conference on Neurosymbolic Learning and Reasoning
summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting enables large language models (LLMs) to tackle multi-step reasoning tasks, yet the generated intermediate steps are not guaranteed to be logically sound. We present Reason Popper-ly, a neurosymbolic framework that uses inductive logic programming (ILP) to learn relation composition rules from reasoning traces and deploys them as an online verifier for step-level correction. Given an LLM-generated trace, the method checks each inferred step against the learned rule table, diagnoses the violation type, rewrites incorrect steps with symbolically derived repairs, and regenerates the remaining suffix so that the model can produce its final answer conditioned on a verified trace. We evaluate on CLUTRR, a multi-hop kinship reasoning benchmark, using five language models over reasoning chains of 2 to 10 hops. Across all models, Reason Popper-ly consistently improves terminal accuracy over standard CoT, with gains of up to 48 percentage points for small models and 15 points for frontier models on the longest chains. Compared with a fully exogenous symbolic pipeline, our method performs better on harder instances by preserving the model's successful grounding while correcting only verifiable reasoning failures. In addition, step-level ILP verification yields a fine-grained error taxonomy that provides diagnostic insight beyond final-answer accuracy.

AI.tldr: Reason Popper-ly is a neurosymbolic framework that uses inductive logic programming to learn relation composition rules from LLM reasoning traces and verifies/repairs incorrect steps in real-time to improve multi-hop reasoning accuracy.
AI.motivation: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting helps LLMs with multi-step reasoning, the intermediate steps generated are not guaranteed to be logically sound, leading to potential reasoning failures that affect final accuracy.
AI.method: The framework uses inductive logic programming (ILP) to learn relation composition rules from reasoning traces, then deploys them as an online verifier. For each LLM-generated trace, it checks steps against learned rules, diagnoses violation types, rewrites incorrect steps with symbolic repairs, and regenerates the remaining suffix for the model to produce final answers from verified traces.
AI.result: Evaluated on CLUTRR (multi-hop kinship reasoning) with 5 language models over 2-10 hop chains. Consistently improved terminal accuracy over standard CoT with gains up to 48 percentage points for small models and 15 points for frontier models on longest chains. Outperformed fully exogenous symbolic pipelines on harder instances by preserving successful model grounding while correcting only verifiable reasoning failures.
AI.conclusion: The neurosymbolic approach of Reason Popper-ly effectively combines LLM strengths with symbolic verification, providing both accuracy improvements and fine-grained error taxonomy for diagnostic insights beyond final-answer metrics.

title: The Intruder Threshold: A Spectral Law for LoRA Fine-Tuning
summary: LoRA fine-tuning can create intruder dimensions: new leading singular vectors of the updated weight matrix $W+BA$ that are nearly orthogonal to all pretrained singular vectors and that drive catastrophic forgetting. Since their discovery, no theory has predicted, layer by layer on measured spectra, when they appear. We derive a per-layer critical update strength $s^\ast=\barθ/(γσ_1(BA))$, computed from the measured spectrum of $W$ alone through the rectangular spiked-deformation transform, together with an exact secular-equation characterization of the updated spectrum, with no fitted parameters. In a pre-specified study spanning four dense Transformer families, a state-space model, a mixture-of-experts model, and an encoder-decoder (18 adapters, 9{,}840 layer scans), the law localizes the empirical threshold within a factor of two on $82\%$ of layers, separates intruder-bearing from intruder-free layers at deployment with a mean AUC of $0.89$, holds unchanged on six third-party adapters, and predicts where WikiText-2 perplexity begins to degrade; a combination of the two pre-specified edge evaluations reaches $98\%$ and is confirmed out-of-bag on the external adapters ($0.997$). Full fine-tuning disperses its update far below the threshold of every layer, which resolves the asymmetry between LoRA and full fine-tuning. Norm-matched interventions confirm that threshold-crossing layers, rather than update magnitude, carry the forgetting, and a spike-budget rule derived from the thresholds, requiring one SVD and no validation sweeps, reduces forgetting by $62\%$ on the most fragile model at no task cost.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a theory predicting when LoRA fine-tuning creates "intruder dimensions" that cause catastrophic forgetting, deriving per-layer critical update thresholds from weight spectra without fitted parameters, validated across diverse model architectures.
AI.motivation: LoRA fine-tuning can create "intruder dimensions" - new singular vectors nearly orthogonal to pretrained ones that drive catastrophic forgetting. While observed empirically, there's been no theoretical framework to predict when they appear layer-by-layer based on measured spectra.
AI.method: Derives per-layer critical update strength formula s*=θ̄/(γσ₁(BA)) computed from pretrained weight W's spectrum via rectangular spiked-deformation transform, with exact secular-equation characterization of updated spectrum. Validated across four dense Transformer families, state-space model, mixture-of-experts, encoder-decoder (18 adapters, 9,840 layer scans).
AI.result: Theory localizes empirical threshold within factor of 2 on 82% of layers, separates intruder-bearing from intruder-free layers with mean AUC 0.89, holds on third-party adapters, predicts WikiText-2 perplexity degradation. Norm-matched interventions show threshold-crossing causes forgetting. Spike-budget rule reduces forgetting by 62% at no task cost.
AI.conclusion: Provides first predictive theory for LoRA intruder dimensions, enabling detection/prevention of catastrophic forgetting through simple spectral analysis without validation sweeps. Explains asymmetry between LoRA and full fine-tuning and offers practical deployment guidelines.

title: Stress-testing large language model agents in a robotic chemistry laboratory
summary: AI is evaluated through knowledge, reasoning and plan generation, yet scientific agency requires reliable physical action and adaptation to evidence. Here, we use a robotic chemistry laboratory as a physical-world testbed to make scientific agency measurable. Its 45 modular workstations exposed as machine-readable skills enabled 4,608 trials. Only 3.3% of trials produced expert-assessed executable workflows under laboratory constraints; even the best system achieved 28.1%. Long-horizon planning remained a challenge: only three executable workflows exceeded 30 operations, although the longest contained 44. Across five rounds, experimental feedback prompted local adjustments but no workflow-level replanning or analytical-method redesign. By making physical executability and evidence-driven replanning measurable, our study provides an evidence-based assessment of deployment readiness and a diagnostic framework to guide closed-loop improvements towards physically grounded autonomous research.

AI.tldr: Robotic chemistry lab testbed reveals current AI scientific agency limitations: only 3.3% of 4,608 trials produced executable workflows under lab constraints, with best system achieving 28.1% success, showing challenges in long-horizon planning and evidence-driven replanning.
AI.motivation: AI evaluation typically focuses on knowledge, reasoning, and plan generation, but lacks physical-world testing for scientific agency. There's a need to measure AI's ability to perform reliable physical actions and adapt to experimental evidence in real-world scientific settings.
AI.method: Used a robotic chemistry laboratory with 45 modular workstations exposed as machine-readable skills, conducting 4,608 trials. Tested AI systems' ability to generate executable workflows under laboratory constraints, tracking physical executability and evidence-driven replanning.
AI.result: Only 3.3% of trials produced expert-assessed executable workflows; best system achieved 28.1% success. Long-horizon planning was challenging (only 3 workflows exceeded 30 operations, max 44). Experimental feedback led to local adjustments but no workflow-level replanning or analytical-method redesign.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a physical-world testbed for measuring scientific agency, offering an evidence-based assessment of deployment readiness and a diagnostic framework to guide closed-loop improvements toward physically grounded autonomous research.

title: Outcome-Confounded Local Supervision in On-Policy Distillation
summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own trajectories while a teacher supplies dense token-level likelihoods at student-visited prefixes. These likelihoods are often read locally: agreement appears safe to imitate, whereas disagreement appears to identify an error. We show that both readings are confounded by the outcome of the completed trajectory. We introduce an outcome-resolved diagnostic that crosses pointwise teacher-student divergence with final-answer correctness, separating safe imitation, productive divergence, harmful divergence, and agreement-on-failure. In an eight-seed mathematical-reasoning study with a Qwen3-8B student and Qwen3-32B teacher, agreement-on-failure constitutes 67.84% of pooled response-token mass; with a Qwen2.5-7B/32B pair it remains 67.68%. The result persists across threshold, sequence-level, format, and truncation audits. Even on prompts that the Qwen3 teacher solves in all four independent attempts, student accuracy rises to 86.91% but agreement-on-failure remains 14.76%. We then run three matched training probes that use the available signals to imitate, mask, or contrast whole trajectories; none consistently reduces agreement-on-failure. The result points to a localization limitation: local divergence paired with a trajectory-level outcome does not identify where a failed trajectory became unrecoverable. Addressing this limitation requires additional positional information, such as process labels, teacher continuations from student prefixes, or token-level alignment across rollouts. Our contribution is therefore diagnostic rather than a new training method.

AI.tldr: The paper reveals that on-policy distillation is confounded by trajectory outcomes, showing that most teacher-student agreement occurs on failed trajectories (agreement-on-failure), and this persists even with various mitigation attempts.
AI.motivation: On-policy distillation (OPD) traditionally assumes that teacher-student agreement indicates safe imitation while disagreement identifies errors, but this reading is confounded by whether the completed trajectory ultimately succeeds or fails.
AI.method: The authors introduce an outcome-resolved diagnostic that crosses pointwise teacher-student divergence with final-answer correctness, creating a 2x2 matrix separating four categories: safe imitation, productive divergence, harmful divergence, and agreement-on-failure. They conduct extensive mathematical reasoning studies with different model pairs (Qwen3-8B/32B, Qwen2.5-7B/32B) and run training probes using available signals.
AI.result: Agreement-on-failure constitutes ~68% of pooled response-token mass across different model pairs, persisting across various audits. Even when the teacher solves prompts in all attempts, student accuracy rises to 86.91% but agreement-on-failure remains at 14.76%. Training probes using imitation, masking, or contrast techniques fail to consistently reduce agreement-on-failure.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals a localization limitation: local divergence paired with trajectory-level outcomes cannot identify where failed trajectories became unrecoverable. Addressing this requires additional positional information like process labels, teacher continuations, or token-level alignment across rollouts. The contribution is diagnostic rather than proposing a new training method.

title: SymStep: Symbolic Step Verification for Logical Reasoning
summary: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting can fail severely on constraint-dense logical reasoning tasks, where unverified errors accumulate silently across steps.
